title: Completed scalar chain model and preservation under inverse image
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an embedding $\iota:E\to L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism with $\ell$ invertible at every stalk [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the specified completed coefficient inclusion and transported inverse images $G_E,G_L$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For every flat-term K-flat $R_Y$-complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $G_EP$, $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$ and $Z=G_EP\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ are flat-term K-flat. There is a natural chain isomorphism $b_P:Z\simeq G_LQ$ carrying $c_L(s)\otimes x$ to $s\otimes x$ on corresponding local sections. Tensors are the specified sheafified balanced tensor, scalar first [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This statement asserts no finite quotient square and no derived comparison.

proof.text: Compose the two maps from inverse image of the completed E coefficient ring into the completed L coefficient ring with every finite projection. The projection formula for inverseImageCompletedCoefficientMap, naturality of the finite constant coefficient comparisons, and the residue formula for completedCoefficientMap make these composites equal. Joint monicity of the limit projections gives the coefficient square. Apply limitScalarChainComparison to the finite E and L coefficient towers. Identify its scalar-extension functors with completedOrdinaryScalarExtension using their specified object equalities to sheafified changeOfRings and their conjugated map equalities. These object equalities give natural isomorphisms, and their inverses transport the sheafification-unit pure tensors to completedScalarTensorSection. Transport the comparison through these isomorphisms and restrict to good complexes. Its forward pure-tensor rule is exactly CompletedFormula. The isomorphism of sites is exact and tensor compatible, so the ringed-topos K-flat pullback theorem applies to inverse image with its transported completed coefficient action. Apply the same theorem to the identity topos and each completed coefficient inclusion to show that ordinary extension preserves flat terms and K-flatness. This gives all three clauses of PreservesModels. The argument applies to unbounded complexes, including the zero complex and an empty site, and requires no flatness of the coefficient inclusion.
